package.b10_source:
DeForest's labor & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is fundamental to business continuity. Acting as strategic counsel to multinational and domestic companies, the team combines labor advisory, litigation, collective labor relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance into a fully integrated national platform capable of supporting complex operations throughout Mexico.
Rather than approaching labor law as a reactive discipline, the practice helps employers anticipate labor risk, strengthen governance frameworks and preserve operational continuity throughout the entire employment lifecycle—from hiring and day-to-day advisory to collective bargaining, workforce restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security matters and high-value litigation.
The practice has developed particular strength advising companies operating in highly regulated and labor-intensive industries, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services, where employment strategy directly affects production continuity, investment certainty and long-term business performance.
The department is led by one of the country's most experienced labor teams. Eduardo Garduño has become one of Mexico's leading labor strategists for multinational employers, combining more than two decades of experience advising major corporations with senior public-sector insight that enables him to translate complex regulatory environments into practical business solutions.
Jaime Bustamante contributes the perspective of one of the region's largest employers, having previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, where he oversaw workforce structures across multiple jurisdictions.
Raymundo Carreño brings the institutional knowledge accumulated during nearly four decades as General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México, offering clients strategic judgement developed through some of the country's most significant labor negotiations and organisational transformations.
The leadership team is further strengthened by Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose practice focuses on labor compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, recognised for his experience in labor litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm's labor practice across the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, a specialist in complex litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, whose practice combines labor, social security and administrative litigation in highly regulated industries.
Today the practice advises employers whose combined workforce exceeds one million employees throughout Mexico. Its work extends well beyond litigation management and encompasses nationwide litigation portfolios involving hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labor disputes managed by the firm's Puebla team. The practice also advises on collective bargaining negotiations, union representation disputes, labor integration following mergers and acquisitions, employer restructurings, labor and social security audits, constitutional litigation, preventive governance programmes and regulatory inspections before the Ministry of Labor, IMSS and INFONAVIT.
Clients consistently retain DeForest not simply to resolve labor disputes, but to preserve organisational stability in environments where workforce disruption could directly affect production, investment and corporate reputation. This preventive, business-oriented philosophy has positioned the practice among Mexico's leading advisers to multinational employers navigating increasingly sophisticated labor challenges.
During the last twelve months alone, the team has also assisted more than twenty clients in connection with labor inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and has handled numerous audits involving labor and social security compliance, reinforcing its position as trusted counsel for employers operating in highly regulated sectors.
The firm's sustained growth is reflected in its recognition by Chambers Latin America 2025 for General Business Law (Querétaro), The Legal 500 since 2024 for labor & Employment and IFLR1000 2025 for Corporate & M&A, confirming the continued consolidation of DeForest as one of Mexico's most sophisticated full-service business law firms.

lawyers.bio:
Eduardo is the Partner of DeForest’s Labor & Employment practice and one of the most respected voices in labor governance in Mexico. His background blends more than two decades advising multinational employers with senior public-sector experience, allowing him to translate complex regulatory environments into stable operational frameworks. He is known for structuring policies and documentation systems that support high-risk, labor-intensive operations, as well as for steering high-value disputes that require strategic judgement and procedural precision. His leadership extends across mandates involving litigation coordination, cross-state governance and preventive frameworks for clients such as Volkswagen, Cinemex, GeNi, Scheaffler, Benteler, SKF and Megacable.
He regularly delivers conferences on labor developments and legal updates at CLAUZ, CANACINTRA and the American Chamber of Commerce in Guadalajara, as well as at universities including Universidad Anáhuac Puebla.
He serves as President of the labor Committee of ANADE Puebla and actively participates in various labor forums, including business chambers.

matters.summary:
Mextypsa, one of Mexico's leading engineering and infrastructure companies, relies on DeForest as its strategic labor counsel for projects where workforce governance is fundamental to successful execution. The firm's mandate extends beyond day-to-day employment advice, encompassing the design of labor structures capable of supporting large-scale infrastructure projects while preserving regulatory compliance and operational continuity throughout each project's lifecycle.

One of the most significant engagements involved the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million infrastructure development requiring a sophisticated labor framework to manage project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation under intense public scrutiny. Simultaneously, DeForest represented the client in complex litigation arising from the Coahuila Wind Farm Project, where an adverse labor judgment threatened liabilities exceeding MXN 5.5 million.

Rather than treating these matters as isolated engagements, DeForest developed a comprehensive labor governance strategy combining preventive advisory with high-stakes dispute resolution. The team designed the contractual and compliance architecture supporting the Guadalajara Metro project, supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies and successfully challenged the adverse labor judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the client's procedural rights and reopening the litigation.

Today, the firm manages more than twenty labor disputes for Mextypsa representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million. Through early negotiation strategies and disciplined litigation management, DeForest has consistently reduced financial exposure while protecting operational continuity across the client's infrastructure portfolio.

matters.summary:
Bonatti has entrusted DeForest with the labor governance strategy supporting several of Mexico's largest energy infrastructure projects, where uninterrupted workforce stability is essential to the successful execution of multi-billion-dollar developments. Acting as strategic labor counsel, the firm advises throughout the entire project lifecycle, integrating labor compliance, collective employment matters and litigation strategy into a single governance framework.

The mandate includes the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, the Cuxtal II expansion, the Ojinaga-El Encino Gas Pipeline and strategic operational support for ENI México's energy projects in Tabasco.

DeForest designed and implemented the labor architecture supporting each project, including workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation. Alongside this preventive work, the firm managed more than twenty labor disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately eighty percent.

The team also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to Mexico's strategic energy infrastructure, safeguarding contractual performance, operational continuity and the client's long-term commercial position. Today, DeForest acts not simply as litigation counsel but as a long-term strategic partner supporting some of the country's most critical infrastructure developments.

matters.summary:
Following Schaeffler's global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies, DeForest was appointed to lead one of the most significant post-acquisition labor integration projects currently underway in Mexico. The transaction required the harmonisation of employment structures across multiple manufacturing facilities while ensuring uninterrupted operations throughout the integration process.

The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

Parallel to the integration, DeForest manages thirty-five active labor proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, ensuring that litigation strategy remains fully aligned with the client's unified post-acquisition governance model. Through this combination of workforce integration, compliance and litigation management, the firm has become a long-term strategic adviser supporting one of the world's leading automotive suppliers.

DeForest led the collective bargaining negotiations, rebuilding dialogue between management and union representatives while designing a renewed agreement that balanced operational efficiency with employee expectations. matters.title: Confidential Matter 5
matters.summary:
Nueva Empresa, S.C. engaged DeForest in two high-value wrongful termination proceedings that raised issues extending well beyond financial exposure. Following procedural objections concerning the legal standing of the company's attorney-in-fact, the labor court refused to recognise the company's representation, disregarded its defence and issued an adverse ruling despite the existence of valid notarial documentation confirming the attorney's legal identity.

The dispute presented a significant constitutional question concerning due process, legal certainty and the recognition of legally valid identity changes, creating an important opportunity to clarify procedural standards within Mexico's labor justice system.

DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Beyond the financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million, the matter is significant for reinforcing constitutional protections governing procedural fairness and the legal recognition of identity, establishing an important precedent with broader implications for labor litigation in Mexico.

Rather than relying exclusively on litigation, DeForest designed a parallel mediation strategy running alongside the judicial proceedings. The firm established common valuation criteria, governance-based negotiation parameters and structured settlement mechanisms capable of facilitating constructive dialogue between parties that had previously been unwilling to negotiate.

The strategy ultimately generated a series of favourable settlement agreements that preserved the employee's legitimate interests while significantly reducing systemic exposure for Enerflex and preventing PEMEX from facing joint liability arising from one of the largest labor awards ever issued in Mexico. The matter remains ongoing, with DeForest continuing to coordinate negotiations alongside PEMEX's in-house legal team.

This engagement reflects the firm's ability to resolve disputes where legal complexity, commercial interests and public-sector exposure intersect at the highest level.
